transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-30
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Michael Chen (Redwood AE), Sara Patel (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (CISO - Lighthouse), Claire Hu (VP Eng), Tom Alvarez (Procurement)

[00:00] Michael Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today. I'd like to run through the SIG/CAIQ and call out where we can provide evidence—SOC 2, pen test, architecture diagrams, etc. Sara's on to answer the technical bits.
[00:15] Rajiv Menon: Thanks Michael. High level, we're mostly focused on data residency, encryption, key management, audit logs for compliance, and the SSO integration. Also curious about dedicated/private deployment options for regulated funds.
[00:30] Michael Chen: Totally. We'll call out Dedicated and Private options. Quick note, some of our product names might come across slightly different in the questionnaire (e.g., Redwood Dedicated / Redwood Dedicatede), apologies in advance for any auto transcript naming quirks.
[00:45] Sara Patel: Hi all. On SOC 2 we are Type II, our report covers control environment and encryption at rest/in transit. We can share the redacted report and the control matrix. Also we have pen test summary and remediation tickets.
[01:05] Claire Hu: When you say "we can share" — is that available immediately or do we need an NDA? We have a legal team that needs the raw artifacts in some cases.
[01:18] Michael Chen: Good question. The SOC 2 report and pen test summary we typically provide to customers under standard confidentiality. If you need more detailed evidence we can get that via an NDA or through our secure portal. Tom, procurement, is that acceptable?
[01:33] Tom Alvarez: Yes that's fine. We'll note the controls we care most about. Timeline wise, we'd like to collect all artifacts before our internal vendor committee on Aug 14.
[01:50] Sara Patel: For RBAC/SSO — we support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. Role-based access with custom roles is available; we also integrate with Okta, Azure AD. A couple of customers also use our built-in RBAC for finer grained controls.
[02:10] Rajiv Menon: Do you support session short-living tokens and token revocation if a user is removed?
[02:18] Sara Patel: Yes, session tokens are revocable and we sync status on SCIM de-provisioning. Token lifetime is configurable via policy, and we can provide the SSO flow diagrams.
[02:35] Michael Chen: On audit logs — we keep request-level audit logs with actor, action, timestamp, and resource. Retention is 90 days by default for hosted, and Dedicated/Private can be configured for longer retention and can be exported to your SIEM. We can share sample log extracts (redacted) as evidence.
[02:56] Rajiv Menon: 90 days might not be enough for us; regulatory needs are 3 years for certain records. How do you handle long-term retention?
[03:06] Sara Patel: For Private deployments or Dedicated with the retention add-on we can push logs to your S3/GCS bucket for archival; then you own the retention policy. We'll note that in the SIG answers.
[03:22] Claire Hu: And encryption—are keys customer-managed? KMS? How does that look across hosted vs private?
[03:30] Sara Patel: Great question. We support cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and you can elect to have customer-managed keys (CMKs) in many cases. For hosted there is envelope encryption with provider-managed keys by default and CMK available for enterprise plans. In Private deployments you can connect to your HSM/KMS and we don't have persistent access to raw keys. We'll include the KMS diagrams and key rotation policy. Note: sometimes the transcript spells KV cache as K V cash — ignore that, it's KV cache for LLMs.
[03:58] Michael Chen: On data residency, we have regionally deployed clusters and Private/VPC options. You can pin model hosting and inference to a region, and for regulatory workloads we recommend Private deployment. We'll include our region map in the evidence pack.
[04:14] Tom Alvarez: About the SIG itself — are you going to complete the CAIQ forms or will you provide answers and attachments?
[04:22] Michael Chen: We'll fill out the SIG spreadsheet with our answers and attach evidence links (SOC 2, pen test, architecture diagrams, IAM screenshots). We usually provide a single zip or S3 location. Sara will own the technical attachments.
[04:35] Rajiv Menon: Do you have any documented key separation or access controls for engineers who might have access to infra? We need to make sure there's least privilege.
[04:45] Sara Patel: Yes, we have RBAC with least privilege, separation of duties, and we use VPC controls and vault-based secrets. We also log privileged access and require justification for temporary elevation — we can include our change control and privileged access process docs.
[05:02] Claire Hu: For the pen test, is the full report available or just a summary?
[05:08] Michael Chen: Typically a summary is included in the public pack; the full report is shared under NDA. We can provide CVE mappings and remediation timelines though.
[05:18] Tom Alvarez: Any third party risk—subprocessors? We need a list for our vendor team.
[05:24] Sara Patel: Yes we maintain a subprocessors list and can provide the current roster and flow chart showing data flows to subprocessors. We'll attach that to the SIG answers.
[05:34] Rajiv Menon: There's a SIG question about encryption-in-transit cipher suites and TLS versions—what do you support?
[05:41] Sara Patel: We enforce TLS 1.2 minimum and prefer TLS 1.3 where supported. Cipher suites adhere to industry best practices; we'll paste the list in the answers.
[05:51] Michael Chen: A couple of action items I'm noting: we'll upload the answered SIG spreadsheet, SOC 2 Type II redacted, pen test summary, architecture diagram, KMS docs, sample audit logs.
[06:02] Claire Hu: Great. For the sample logs, can you include an example showing user de-provisioning events so our SIEM can map fields?
[06:10] Sara Patel: Yep we'll include a redacted example with mapping notes (user_id, event_type, timestamp, actor).
[06:20] Rajiv Menon: On legal/compliance, any certifications beyond SOC 2—ISO 27001, or any data residency certifications?
[06:28] Michael Chen: We are pursuing ISO 27001 but not certified yet; we can share the gap assessment and timeline. For certain regions we have partners to help with in-region hosting — details to follow.
[06:40] Tom Alvarez: Procurement question — what's the typical lead time for Private deployment? And costs?
[06:47] Michael Chen: Private deployments vary; typical lead time is 6-8 weeks for VPC/private with dedicated support and onboarding. We'll send a cost ballpark and SOW template. That will go to you after this call.
[06:58] Claire Hu: Are there any known limitations around model quantization and inference accuracy when using private/offline stacks? Just for our SE to note.
[07:06] Sara Patel: Some quantization profiles can affect output distribution; we provide recommended profiles per model and workload. For Private we can test and lock a quantization profile during the POC so you get reproducible results.
[07:20] Michael Chen: Let's go over the timeline: we'll upload the completed SIG and evidence by Aug 4; you (Lighthouse) will review and provide any follow-up questions by Aug 8; we'll reconvene Aug 12 to go over SOC 2 and pen test details with legal. Anything to add?
[07:36] Rajiv Menon: That works. Please include the evidence links in a single location. Also call out any exceptions in the SIG answers explicitly.
[07:44] Michael Chen: Will do. One last note — competitors were mentioned during procurement: VendorX and CloudProviderAI. If there are any direct comparisons you want us to address, flag them and we'll provide direct mapping.
[07:58] Tom Alvarez: We'll flag any specific questions. Thanks Michael and Sara.
[08:05] Michael Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the SIG spreadsheet and evidence. See you on the 12th.

Notes about transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (KV cache -> K V cash), some speaker labels may shift; this is raw Fireflies export style text.
